title: Fly the average, not the last step: the exported model is the uniform average of the weights visited over the second half of training (SWAD/SWA-style dense weight averaging), with BatchNorm statistics recalibrated for the averaged weights
hypothesis: Every architectural lever this era pulled has been the trunk, and the size gate now closes that road: experiment 19's export is 31.7 MB against a 32 MiB (33.6 MB) fp32 ceiling, so a bigger or third trunk cannot be added. What remains on the held-out truedop_2024 photograph is 6.5% abstention and 1.0% false fixes (usable 92.5%, mission 0.085), while the three training photographs read 100% usable / 0% false at the same held-out viewpoints: the residual is entirely the survey gap. A never-seen photograph is a shift of the input distribution, and the domain-generalisation literature is consistent on what a training procedure can do about such a shift with no extra capacity: the solution found by SGD's last iterate sits in a sharp region whose loss rises quickly under shift, while the average of the weights visited along the late trajectory sits in a flatter, wider minimum whose test loss rises much more slowly (SWA, Izmailov et al. UAI 2018; SWAD, Cha et al. NeurIPS 2021, which made dense weight averaging the strongest single domain-generalisation method on DomainBed, consistently beating ERM by 1.5-3 points out-of-domain, with gains concentrated in the shifted domains rather than the in-domain ones). That is exactly our split: in-domain is saturated (100%), out-of-domain is 92.5%. Nothing in 19 experiments of this era, nor any of the 83 earlier ones (searched: no EMA/SWA/weight-averaging row in lineage_history), has changed WHICH point of the trajectory is flown; every export is the last iterate of an 8-epoch run whose loss was still falling (6.16 -> 5.40 over epochs 5-8) and whose learning rate never drops below 0.1x, so the last iterate is still being kicked around by single-batch noise. Averaging is also the natural partner of the committee gate: frames abstain when one member's belief on the consensus block falls below 0.3, and a flatter member's softmax moves less when the photograph changes, so frames currently lost to one member wobbling should convert to usable fixes. Builds on experiment 19 (the champion) unchanged in architecture.
method: model/train.py only: keep a running UNIFORM average of every member parameter, updated every AVG_EVERY = 4 optimiser steps from the first step of epoch AVG_START_EPOCH = epochs // 2 + 1 (epoch 5 of 8) to the end of training (~13.6k steps -> ~3.4k snapshots). After the last epoch, load the averaged parameters into the model, recalibrate every BatchNorm layer's running statistics for the averaged weights with one no-grad pass of BN_RECAL_BATCHES = 400 augmented paired-survey training batches (cumulative averaging, momentum=None), and export THAT model. The architecture, deployed graph, losses, augmentation, schedule, epochs and optimiser are unchanged.
expected_outcome: Predicted on truedop_2024: mission 0.085 -> ~0.055-0.070; usable_fix_rate 92.5% -> ~94-95% (most of the gain from abstentions converting to usable fixes as the committee members' beliefs become more stable under the survey shift), false_fix_rate staying at or below 1.0%, abstain_rate 6.5% -> ~4-5%. train_capture_diagnostics should stay at ~100% usable (an average of good late-trajectory points is not worse in-domain); median error ~36 m roughly unchanged. Model size and latency identical (same graph, same parameter count). Refutation: usable on 2024 flat or down with the train diagnostics unchanged would say the residual survey gap is not a sharpness/flatness effect, and that the last 7.5% must be bought with new information (data or capacity), not with a better point on the same trajectory. If the survey_diag logged on the averaged model shows higher xs_cos_same / xsurvey_agree than the last iterate's but 2024 does not move, that also is informative and should be recorded.
init_strategy: pretrained:efficientnet_b0 IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..7] (torchvision, Apache-2.0 weights), fine-tuned at 0.1x LR — unchanged from experiment 19
eli5: Training a model is like a hiker wandering downhill in fog: where they happen to be standing at the moment we stop is a bit random, and often on a narrow ledge where a small change in the ground (a new photograph of the city) sends them tumbling. Instead of keeping the hiker's last footprint, we average all the spots they stood on during the second half of the walk. That average lands in the middle of a broad, flat valley, so a photograph taken in a different year, season or light moves the model's answer less. The drone carries exactly the same size of model; only the choice of which version we ship has changed.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: the 128 px frame is enlarged to 224 px and read by two independent copies of EfficientNet-B0 (pre-trained on ImageNet, Apache-2.0), fine-tuned on Berlin; each reads a 112-channel 14×14 map and a 320-channel 7×7 map, each lifted to 56 numbers and averaged over the frame into a 112-number place description. NOW: the weights carried are the average of the many versions visited over the second half of training, not the last one

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor's description is centred, scaled to unit length and compared by angle against one unit-length reference direction per map tile (~3,000 tiles, 128 m each); the angle match times a fixed sharpness (30) is the tile score. The two members' tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: weight averaging. Training is unchanged (cross-survey style mixing, angular-margin tile loss, offset loss, paired three-survey batches, re-photographing augmentation, pre-trained blocks at a tenth of the learning rate, 8 epochs), but from the start of epoch 5 a running average of every weight is kept, updated every 4 steps; at the end the model takes the averaged weights, its normalisation statistics are re-measured on 400 training batches, and that averaged model is what flies

implementation_brief:
ONE file changes: model/train.py. model/model.py is NOT touched (no constant, no graph change). Do not open, list or load the eval capture in any form; everything below reads only the training captures already on the device in `scene`.

1. Constants near the top of train.py:
   AVG_EVERY = 4            # optimiser steps between weight snapshots
   BN_RECAL_BATCHES = 400   # augmented training batches used to re-measure BN stats of the averaged model
   The start epoch is computed in train_area as `avg_start = epochs // 2` (0-based; = epoch 5 of 8, 1-based); for epochs == 1 this gives 0, i.e. averaging over the whole run, which is fine.

2. A small class `WeightAverager` in train.py:
   - __init__(self, model): self.params = [p for p in model.parameters()] (same order every time); self.avg = None; self.n = 0 (Python int); self.step = 0 (Python int).
   - maybe_update(self): increments self.step; if self.step % AVG_EVERY != 0 return. On the first snapshot: self.avg = [p.detach().clone() for p in self.params]; self.n = 1. Otherwise self.n += 1 and `torch._foreach_lerp_(self.avg, [p.detach() for p in self.params], 1.0 / self.n)` (uniform running mean). If _foreach_lerp_ is unavailable on the device, fall back to a per-tensor loop `a.lerp_(p.detach(), 1.0 / self.n)`. NO .item()/.cpu()/float() on device tensors — self.n and self.step are Python ints, so nothing stalls the GPU queue.
   - copy_to(self, model): with torch.no_grad(): for p, a in zip(model.parameters(), self.avg): p.copy_(a).
   Average PARAMETERS only, never buffers (BN running stats are re-measured, step 4).

3. run_epoch gets one extra keyword argument `averager=None`; immediately after `opt.step()` add `if averager is not None: averager.maybe_update()`. Nothing else in the step loop changes.

4. In train_area: build `averager = WeightAverager(model)` after the optimiser. In the epoch loop pass `averager=(averager if epoch >= avg_start else None)`. Keep the per-epoch survey_diag and the log line exactly as they are (they measure the LAST ITERATE). After the loop:
   a. Record `last_diag = diag` (last-iterate diagnostic).
   b. Guard: if averager.avg is None (e.g. a tiny timing run), skip averaging and log that it was skipped; otherwise averager.copy_to(model).
   c. BN recalibration, function `recalibrate_bn(model, scene, crop_xy, meta, rng, device, n_caps, pos_per_chunk, n_batches)`: for every nn.BatchNorm1d/BatchNorm2d module m in model: remember m.momentum, call m.reset_running_stats(), set m.momentum = None (cumulative average). model.train() (so BN uses batch stats and updates running stats; MixStyle and stochastic depth behave as in training — identical conditions to how the champion's own running stats were accumulated). Under torch.no_grad(), draw batches exactly like run_epoch does: chunk_views over a fresh rng permutation of the lattice, gpu_crops, then for EACH member its own augment_views draw and `member(xb_k)` (forward only, same cuda-only bf16 autocast as run_epoch; outputs discarded). Stop after n_batches batches of BATCH_SIZE. Then restore each BN module's original momentum. Do not call opt.step(); do not touch any parameter. Use the same `rng` object (it is the run's numpy Generator) so the run stays seeded.
   d. Run `avg_diag = survey_diag(...)` on the averaged, recalibrated model and print one log line `[area] averaged model: n_snapshots=<n> from epoch <avg_start+1> every <AVG_EVERY> steps, bn_recal_batches=<N> xs_cos_same=... xs_cos_diff=... wpv=... xsurvey_agree=... clean_top1=...` plus the same five fields of last_diag for comparison.
   e. Export the AVERAGED model with the existing `export_onnx(model.cpu(), str(onnx_path))` to the same path <out>/models/<area>.onnx. Do not write any other .onnx file.

5. train_info dict: keep every existing key. `final_xs_cos_same`, `final_wpv`, `final_xsurvey_agree`, `final_clean_top1`, `final_xs_cos_diff` now come from avg_diag (the model that is exported); add `last_iterate_xs_cos_same`, `last_iterate_wpv`, `last_iterate_xsurvey_agree`, `last_iterate_clean_top1` from last_diag, plus `weight_averaging: {"kind": "uniform SWA/SWAD-style parameter average", "start_epoch_1based": avg_start+1, "every_steps": AVG_EVERY, "n_snapshots": averager.n, "bn_recalibration_batches": BN_RECAL_BATCHES, "buffers": "re-measured, not averaged"}`. Append ", uniform weight average over the second half of training with BN recalibration (exported)" to the `capture_sampling` string. Update the module docstring with a short WEIGHT AVERAGING (experiment 20) paragraph in the existing style.

CONTRACTS TO PRESERVE (the frozen scorer depends on them): train.py's CLI is unchanged (`python -m model.train --area <a> --out-dir <d> [--data-dir] [--epochs] [--max-crops-per-bucket] [--seed]`), it writes <out-dir>/models/<area>.onnx and appends to <out-dir>/train_info.json. The ONNX export contract in model/model.py's docstring is unchanged: input 'frame' 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1] -> output 'uvc' [[u, v, conf]], u/v normalised map coords, conf in [0,1], whole decode inside the graph, export via the existing export_onnx (opset 17, dynamo=False). Parameter count and graph are identical to experiment 19, so size (31.7 MB, gate 32 MiB) and latency are unchanged — do NOT add parameters, members or buffers to the model. Training reads only buckets(meta, "train"); nothing under model/ may open truedop_2024. Keep all device work on the device (no per-step host syncs). Cost: the averaging adds ~1 foreach op every 4 steps and the recalibration ~400 forward-only batches (~2-3% of one epoch); total wall-clock essentially unchanged.
